findings.quote: Representatives serve $3$ years, with at most $3$ consecutive terms (Section $7$). Consecutive means in a row, not a lifetime total. For both Houses, Article VI, Sections $4$ and $7$ state: "Voluntary renunciation of the office for any length of time shall not be considered as an interruption in the continuity of his service for the full term for which he was elected." This means choosing to give up the office does not break the term count.

The lesson defines branch powers, bill, origination, appropriation, veto, override and all Members before application. Emergency powers introduce martial law and the writ before their limits. Judicial review, en banc and the Judicial and Bar Council are defined before examples.

Qualification teaching defines natural-born citizenship, Bar membership, collegiate courts, judicial character terms, CPA and auditing. The citizenship special case and CSC row are expressly referred to named lessons; neither is needed to solve the supplied cases.

Congress is taught through lawmaking, origination, inquiry, appropriation and voting rules; executive power through control, appointments, succession and bounded emergency/clemency powers; judicial power through actual disputes and review of unconstitutional acts.

Officer eligibility compares ages, citizenship, residence, experience, professional mix and prior candidacy. Checks and balances identify the acting body and its limiting power. The lesson teaches these concepts locally instead of relying on bare prerequisite names.

House size includes the unless-law-fixes-otherwise qualification; term limits distinguish consecutive terms from lifetime totals and address voluntary renunciation. District voter/residence requirements exclude party-list representatives.

Emergency power requires invasion or rebellion plus public safety, includes initial duration, reporting, revocation, extension, judicial review and detention safeguards. Pardon requires final conviction and excludes impeachment; election clemency and amnesty have their stated concurrence conditions.

Appointment rules distinguish listed executive offices, constitutional commissions, judges and the Vice-President in Cabinet. Judicial review requires a proper case. Age is expressly insufficient alone; lower collegiate courts and other qualifications are distinguished.
